Ingredion approached Penford in July 2014 and made successive proposals beginning at $17.00 per share in August. Penford rejected requests for exclusivity and authorized a market check on August 28. Deutsche Bank contacted six strategic counterparties, of which Parties A, C and D signed confidentiality agreements. The board selected Ingredion for definitive negotiations on October 3 while Deutsche Bank continued seeking an offer from Party A. Party A ultimately offered $16.00 per share, and Ingredion confirmed $19.00 despite lower draft financial results. Penford and Ingredion signed the cash merger on October 14 and announced it the next day.
